newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian shares advance, but no big moves seen.
newsitem.headline: Russian shares advance, but no big moves seen.

text.p: Russian shares inched up on Tuesday led by secondary issues catching up with gains made by the leading shares earlier this year.
Analysts said the market would likely stay flat for the time being as investors assessed the political risk of President Boris Yeltsin's long absence from the Kremlin.
The Russian Trading System 24-share index rose one percent to 279.55 from 276.79 at Monday's close.
Utility company Chelyabenergo CHNG.RTS O#CHNG.RUO rose almost 20 percent for the second day in a row, closing at $0.45 from $0.38 on Monday.
Mosenergo MSNG.RTS O#MSNG.RUO, also a utility company, rose to $1.435 from $1.400. UES rose to $0.1578 from $0.1552 and Irkutskenergo rose to $0.297 from $0.288.
"Investors think Irkutskenergo will follow the same path as Mosenergo did last year, when it issued an ADR and rose five-fold," said Creditanstalt-Grant senior trader Andrei Galperin.
Christopher Smart, Director of Research at Pioneer Securities said the market was not likely to charge ahead in the next few sessions.
"Generally people are waiting for a correction, but nobody seems ready to unload what they bought over the last month," he added.
